title: Product scribe — morning tactical log
content:
2026-03-09 morning log — quick capture (Maya)

Top priorities today:
- Finish PRD edits for token-prefix caching section (inc. failure modes). Need final wording for 'cache invalidation on model switch'.
- Confirm canary rollout % and automated rollback thresholds with SRE (Jonas).
- Send stakeholder note re: latency/regression guardrails (Priya to OK copy).

Meeting notes (standup + sync w/ infra, 09:30):
- Infra reported a potential edge case when requests jump from 10rps -> 600rps for one route: batching fallback triggers but KV cache pressure spikes. Action: add metric for "kv-cache-fill-rate" and surface in console (Ethan to pair with infra).
- Canaries: proposed split = 2% -> 10% over 1h -> 25% after 6h if no regressions. Rollback if 95th-p99 latency increases by >20% or error rate >0.5% absolute.
- Feature flagging: need new toggle "token_cache_v2" with sticky assignment and manual override in Console. Product to own naming and description.

PRD edit checklist (what I changed / still open):
- Added short section: "Failure isolation and graceful degradation" with 3 scenarios: model OOM, KV cache eviction storm, region outage. (open: sample responses for SDK to surface - write examples)
- Clarified the compatibility matrix for quantized model variants (LLM-q4_0 vs q8_1) and latency delta expectations. Need input from runtime bench (Ethan).
- Included monitoring SLOs: token-level p95 latency target per model family. Need legal wording for SLA references.

To-do (short actionable list):
1) Draft stakeholder email summarizing canary plan + key metrics to watch — target to send by 14:00. (Assignee: Maya)
2) Create a small eval prompt set to surface quality regressions for caching path — include existing 12 prompts + 3 new edge prompts. (Assignee: Priya)
3) Add 2 dashboards: "KV cache health" and "Canary rollout health" with thresholds. (Assignee: Jonas)
4) Update PR and add unit tests for cache invalidation on model pin change. (Assignee: eng-owner on PR#1228)
5) Schedule brief playbook read-through with on-call SRE team at 16:00. (Assignee: Maya / Jonas)

Open questions / unresolved:
- If canary triggers rollback, do we want an automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant or a hard stop? Pros/cons listed in notes below — need team decision.
- What exact wording do we want for customer-facing incident messages if a model is auto-failed-over? Keep it non-technical but actionable.
- Does the Dedicated tier get a different rollback SLA? Legal asked for differentiation; product should propose language.

Short draft text for stakeholder email (copy to iterate):
"Hi all — Quick note on today's canary for token-prefix caching (feature flag token_cache_v2). Plan: ramp 2% -> 10% -> 25% with automated rollback triggers on latency/error thresholds. Monitors: p95 latency, error rate, kv-cache-fill-rate. If rollback occurs we will automatically route to the compatible quantized model variant unless SREs opt for freeze. Asking for acknowledgements from infra, runtime, and support. Will post live updates in #deploys. —Maya"

Launch checklist (personal quick ver):
- [ ] PRD final review (language + failure modes)
- [ ] Add dashboard panels + alerts
- [ ] Feature flag created in Console + QA toggle
- [ ] Canary config committed to infra repo
- [ ] Stakeholder note sent + Slack thread pinned
- [ ] Post-mortem template ready (pre-created)

Metrics to watch first 2 hours post-canary (owner in parens):
- p95 token latency (Ethan)
- end-to-end request error rate (Jonas)
- kv-cache-fill-rate and eviction spikes (Ethan)
- cheap-quality-check mismatch rate (Priya)

Notes to self / quick heuristics:
- Keep canary windows small and human-in-the-loop for first run.
- If we see noise across all models, suspect infra/region vs feature-specific.
- Document every manual rollback step in the incident doc as we do it.

Small friction items to raise this afternoon:
- Need an example SDK response shape for 'cache-miss-fallback' (quick snippet).
- Docs: update console tooltip copy for "predictable throughput" claim if caching changes economics.

End-of-day rituals (for myself):
- send short summary to exec-ops if canary reached 25% or if there was rollback.
- mark PRD as 'in_review' or 'final' depending on feedback.
- quick write-up of any manual interventions and timestamps.

Timestamped quick captures:
- 09:45 Jonas (infra): will add kv-cache-fill-rate metric by EOD.
- 10:10 Priya: agreed to assemble 3 new edge prompts for quality checks by 12:00.
- 11:02 Ethan: will run an extended bench for q4_0 vs q8_1 and share numbers by tomorrow morning.

Random note to file away:
- Consider a small UI affordance in Console: "Simulate canary traffic" (local sandbox) — would speed up dev-testing.

-- Maya
